findings.observed: Customization accepts inline system_prompt; provided inline variant is loaded verbatim. Full LSCore HTTP request returned total 11 and the inline output marker with the deterministic model fixture.

The configured Python module imports and loads system_prompts.default and topic_summary. Full LSCore HTTP request returned total 11 and the profile output marker with the deterministic model fixture. CustomProfile exposes only path and prompts. This is prompt loading, not per-step Python execution.

findings.observed: Configured neutral-assessment discovered at runtime. Full LSCore HTTP request successfully invoked list_skills, load_skill, and read_skill_resource; final output contained the expected marker and resource-only token. This proves skill loading and transmission, not real-model compliance with the instructions.
findings.limitation: Pinned docs call two tools activate_skill and load_skill_resource; installed locked pydantic-ai-skills 1.4.0 exposes load_skill and read_skill_resource instead.

findings.capability: Arbitrary deterministic Python branching between model/tool steps via documented LSCore extension
findings.classification: Unsupported through the inspected documented configuration
findings.observed: No registration mechanism found. Customization rejects after_tool_result, capabilities, and agent_factory as unknown fields. Profile loader copies system_prompts only; extra PROFILE_CONFIG callback is not exposed. Agent construction selects a fixed capability set. This does not prove no possible library embedding; embedding a different Agent or monkeypatching LSCore is outside this experiment.
findings.follow_up: Ask LSCore maintainers whether a supported custom capability or per-step callback registration exists outside the inspected guide/configuration.

findings.observed: run_skill_script explicitly excluded in LSCore helper and absent from runtime skill tools. Skill scripts cannot provide the required loop callback.

scope_limits: No upstream source patched or monkeypatched.
Direct capability invocation proves loading only, not real-model instruction compliance.
Built-in shields support specific safety checks but do not expose an arbitrary Python branching entry point.
Underlying Pydantic AI supports capabilities; that alone does not establish LSCore supports registering application-defined ones.
